tool.name: AddRandomNumbers

summary.para:
View online help files: https://www.jennessent.com/data-tools/add-random-numbers.html
Fills a numeric field of a layer's or table's records -- only the selected records when there is a selection, and only the records a definition query shows -- with a constant, a random permutation of 1 to N (every record a different number: the classic way to assign treatments to plots at random), the same permutation repeated for each replicate (a case field groups the records, and every group gets its own 1 to n -- made for a Plot Designer output), random integers within a range, random decimals between 0 and 1 or within a range, or draws from a normal distribution with a given mean and standard deviation. A missing field is created (integer or double precision as the values need). A seed makes the result repeatable. A port of the CropCentric Add Random Numbers tool (Jenness and Wiebers 2018). Works at every license level.

tool.usage:
Which records. A map layer or table view writes only the records it shows: its selection, if any, and its definition query are honored. A dataset path writes every record. N, for the permutation, is the number of records written; for the repeated permutation it is the size of each group.
The values: • Constant value -- the same number in every record. • Random permutation of 1 to N -- the numbers 1..N dealt out in random order, each used once (treatment numbers, random plot order, random visit order). • Random permutation of 1 to N (repeated for replicates) -- the records are grouped by the case field (for example the Rep field that Plot Designer writes) and each group is dealt its own permutation of 1..n, n being that group's size: three replicates of a four-plot block get 1..4 three times over, one random order per replicate, not 1..12 once. Records with no value in the case field form a group of their own. • Random integers within a range -- each record an independent whole number from lowest to highest, inclusive (repeats allowed). • Random decimals between 0 and 1 -- uniform on [0, 1). • Random decimals within a range -- uniform between lowest and highest. • Random decimals from a normal distribution -- Gaussian draws with the given mean and standard deviation.
How the numbers are made. Every mode draws from Python's random module, seeded with your seed, so the same seed with the same records reproduces any mode exactly. The uniform numbers underneath come from the Mersenne Twister (Matsumoto and Nishimura 1998), 53 random bits per value. The permutation modes are Fisher-Yates shuffles in Durstenfeld's form (Fisher and Yates 1938; Durstenfeld 1964; Knuth 1997, Algorithm P), each index drawn by rejection sampling, so every ordering is equally likely; the integer range is drawn the same way. The normal mode is the Box-Muller transform in its original trigonometric form (Box and Muller 1958): from two uniform values U1 and U2 it forms cos(2 pi U1) sqrt(-2 ln(1 - U2)) and sin(2 pi U1) sqrt(-2 ln(1 - U2)), two independent standard-normal values used for two successive records, then scaled by the mean and standard deviation. The run messages and the field's metadata record the method used.
References. Box, G. E. P., and M. E. Muller. 1958. A note on the generation of random normal deviates. Annals of Mathematical Statistics 29:610-611. https://doi.org/10.1214/aoms/1177706645. Durstenfeld, R. 1964. Algorithm 235: random permutation. Communications of the ACM 7:420. https://doi.org/10.1145/364520.364540. Fisher, R. A., and F. Yates. 1938. Statistical tables for biological, agricultural and medical research. Oliver and Boyd, Edinburgh, UK. Knuth, D. E. 1997. The art of computer programming, volume 2: seminumerical algorithms. Third edition. Addison-Wesley, Reading, Massachusetts, USA. Matsumoto, M., and T. Nishimura. 1998. Mersenne twister: a 623-dimensionally equidistributed uniform pseudo-random number generator. ACM Transactions on Modeling and Computer Simulation 8:3-30. https://doi.org/10.1145/272991.272995.
The field. The list offers the input's writable numeric fields (the ObjectID and geometry fields are left out); pick an existing field to write the new values in place, or type a name of your own. Integer fields take only the integer modes and whole-number constants. The dialog will stop you if you try to write a decimal number, or a constant with a decimal part, into an integer field. A name that does not exist yet is created as a LONG field for integer values or a DOUBLE field for decimals (shortened to ten characters on a shapefile or dBASE table).
Repeatability. Give a seed to get the same numbers again; leave it empty for a fresh draw each run.

dialogReference.para: The layer, table view, feature class or table whose records are written. A layer's selection and definition query are honored.

param.name: field
param.displayname: Field to fill (pick a numeric field, or type a new field name)

dialogReference.para: The field to write. The list offers the input's writable numeric fields; pick one to fill it in place, or type a name that does not exist yet and it is created (integer or double precision to suit the values). An integer field only takes whole numbers: a decimal mode, or a constant with a decimal part, is refused with a message.

Constant value; Random permutation of 1 to N (each record unique); Random permutation of 1 to N (repeated for replicates); Random integers within a range; Random decimals between 0 and 1; Random decimals within a range; or Random decimals from a normal distribution (mean, standard deviation). The permutations are Fisher-Yates shuffles and the normal values come from the Box-Muller transform, on Mersenne Twister uniforms (see the tool's usage notes for the references).

param.name: case_field
param.displayname: Case field (replicate; each group gets its own permutation)

dialogReference.para: For the repeated-permutation mode: the field whose values identify the replicates (groups). Each distinct value is dealt its own permutation of 1 to n, n being the number of records with that value. A Plot Designer output has it ready-made as Rep, which is suggested when the input has one.
The value for the Constant value mode.
For the range modes (inclusive for integers).

param.name: sd
param.displayname: Standard deviation of the normal distribution

dialogReference.para: For the normal-distribution mode (Box-Muller transform); cannot be negative.

param.name: seed
param.displayname: Random seed (optional; repeats the same numbers)

dialogReference.para: Any whole number: the seed of the Mersenne Twister generator behind every mode. The same seed with the same records gives the same numbers again.
The input, after writing (for ModelBuilder chaining).

scriptExample.title: Add Random Numbers example (stand-alone script)
scriptExample.para: Deal the treatment numbers 1..n afresh within every replicate of a Plot Designer output (its Rep field is the case field).
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your install path arcpy.jenness.AddRandomNumbers( in_table=r"D:\data\trial.gdb\Plots_2026", field="Treatment", mode="Random permutation of 1 to N (repeated for replicates)", case_field="Rep", seed=42)

scriptExample.title: One replicate only
scriptExample.para: Deal 1..N to the selected plots of replication 2 alone.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your install path arcpy.management.MakeFeatureLayer(r"D:\data\trial.gdb\Plots_2026", "plots") arcpy.management.SelectLayerByAttribute("plots", "NEW_SELECTION", "Rep = 2") arcpy.jenness.AddRandomNumbers( in_table="plots", field="Treatment", mode="Random permutation of 1 to N (each record unique)", seed=42)
